issues.description: Regex /\dm?s/i is a loose pre-filter that matches non-time substrings without acknowledgment.
issues.detail: The pattern matches digit+optional-m+s anywhere in the string, so identifiers like 'dims', 'class-3s-foo', or url('a3ms') pass the gate. That is acceptable for a heuristic — the real parser still runs — but the looseness should be explicit, either via a tighter anchor (e.g. \b) or a comment naming it a deliberate over-approximation.

issues.description: No comment naming the invariant behind the fast-path optimization.
issues.detail: A one-line comment stating 'any CSS time value must contain a digit immediately preceding s or ms, so this is a cheap pre-filter for valueParser' would make the optimization self-documenting. Without it, the next maintainer has to reverse-engineer intent from a cryptic regex constant.

issues.description: No regression test pinning the early-return behavior.
issues.detail: The patch is behavior-preserving in theory, but a targeted test for edge cases (vendor prefixes, odd whitespace, mixed case like 'MS') would lock the fast-path against future regressions where the regex accidentally rejects a real violation. Not blocking, but cheap insurance for a hot-path change.

issues.description: Performance change ships with no benchmark numbers in the changeset.
issues.detail: The PR is framed as a perf fix but the changeset states no before/after timing and no invariant. Documenting the measured speedup and the precise set of values the fast-path provably skips would make the optimization auditable rather than asserted.

synthesis.summary: The panel accepts this as a small, well-scoped optimization: a cheap regex pre-filter that short-circuits the expensive valueParser path while leaving the real parser as the source of truth. The decomposition is clean and the diff matches surrounding style. The shared concern is honesty about the heuristic — the regex /\dm?s/i is a deliberate over-approximation that matches non-time substrings, and neither the code nor the changeset names this invariant. Recommended fixups: add a one-line comment explaining the pre-filter, consider a tighter anchor, and ideally add a regression test plus benchmark numbers. Verdict: ACCEPT with trivial cleanups.
